criterion_notes.c1: Examines household access to public water supply services (WSS) in the Federal District of Brazil, focusing on economic affordability (water poverty), connection rates, and residential water consumption across service areas.
criterion_notes.c2: Satisfies BOTH the plain wording and the narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type reading of Criterion 2. Plain reading: examines regulatory pricing and utility governance instruments (CAESB water tariff schedules regulated by ADASA, situated within Brazil's Basic Sanitation Legal Framework Law 11,445/2007 and Law 14,026/2020). Narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type reading: directly examines 'tariff or cost-recovery rules' governing service access—specifically the increasing block tariff (IBT) structure, lifeline block volume and price thresholds (2019 vs. 2020/2021 tariff reform), connection fees, cross-subsidy incidence rules, and social tariff coverage.
criterion_notes.c3: Quantitative empirical study combining utility/regulatory tariff, billing, connection, cost, and residential water consumption records (2019 and 2020/2021) with local household survey microdata (Codeplan 2018), using Komives et al. (2005) subsidy-targeting decomposition (Omega) and multivariable binary logistic regression.
criterion_notes.c4: Reports quantitative outcomes on household water affordability / water poverty (share of household income > 3% committed to water bills at the lifeline block and at 7, 10, 20, and 30 m3/month), subsidy benefit incidence (Omega and its connection and consumption components), and per-capita/household water consumption.
criterion_notes.c5: Population and units of analysis (households / residential consumer units across Service Areas served by CAESB in the Federal District of Brazil; total units reported across 6 SA income groups in Table 2), exposure (2019 vs. 2020/2021 IBT water tariff structure, lifeline block, connection fee, cross-subsidy rules, and household socioeconomic characteristics under the tariff schedule), outcome (water poverty >3% income commitment, Omega subsidy targeting ratio, residential consumption), and quantitative observational study design are all clearly identifiable.
criterion_notes.c6: Full text is written in English, an eligible review language.

evidence_quotes.quote: The study aims to investigate if the current subsidies’ strategy used in the FDB is in fact promoting the necessary conditions of affordability in regions where physical access to water is already in place.

The data used are the water utility tariff structure, residential water consumption, number of household units in each water volume range of the IBT framework considering the WSS tariff structure in force in 2019 and 2021, and the average costs of public WSS. This data set was combined with socioeconomic and demographic information from a local household survey.

We applied a binary logistic model to identify the variables associated with the probability of water poverty occurrence (deﬁned as income commitment greater than 3%) for consumption in the lifeline block of a tariff structure.

Analysis of the economic affordability of WSS services showed that the change in the tariff structure that took place in 2020/2021 was minimally effective in reducing the average income commitment for access to water.

The regressivity of the Ω indicator was motivated mostly due to the connection rate for lower-income SA, such as SCIA and Fercal. Additionally, the amount of subsidized water consumption was higher in the higher-income regions, such as Lago Sul and Plano Piloto.

raw_response.exposure: Water supply utility tariff and cross-subsidy rules (Increasing Block Tariff [IBT] volume/price blocks, 2019 vs. 2020/2021 lifeline block restructuring, connection fees, and social tariff coverage) interacting with household socioeconomic and demographic characteristics
raw_response.outcome: Household economic affordability / water poverty (income commitment > 3% for water consumption in the lifeline block and at 7, 10, 20, and 30 m3/month), subsidy targeting performance (Omega indicator and connection/consumption/beneficiary ratios), and residential water consumption volume
raw_response.population_and_sample: Households and residential consumer units across Service Areas (SAs) served by CAESB in the Federal District of Brazil (approximately 1,141,984 total residential consumer units across 6 SA income groups in Table 2, combined with local household survey microdata from Codeplan 2018)
raw_response.rationale: This empirical quantitative study evaluates how utility water tariff and cross-subsidy rules (increasing block tariffs, lifeline block thresholds, connection fees, and the 2019 to 2020/2021 tariff reform) in the Federal District of Brazil govern household water affordability, subsidy incidence, and water poverty. It directly examines tariff and cost-recovery rules governing service access under both the plain wording and the narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type reading of Criterion 2, uses primary/administrative utility data linked with household survey microdata, and reports clear affordability, connection-ratio, subsidy-incidence, and consumption outcomes. All inclusion criteria (c1-c6) are satisfied.
raw_response.study_design: Quantitative observational study combining pre/post tariff-reform utility billing/consumption records (2019 and 2020/2021) and household survey microdata, using subsidy-incidence decomposition (Omega) and multivariable binary logistic regression
